CRESTING THE RIDGE — striding upright onto a wind-scoured ridgeline, pack settled across her shoulders, one hand shielding her eyes as she reads the valley below, the trail still humming in her legs, horizon finally cracking open ahead.

CREEK REFILL — crouched low at a rushing stream bank, waterskin submerged and bubbling, free hand steadying herself on a mossy stone, late-afternoon gold cutting through the canopy, the sound of moving water the only noise for miles.

STEALTH ADVANCE — moving forward in a low, deliberate crouch along a shadowed forest floor, short sword drawn and angled low, eyes locked on a dark gap between the tree-trunks ahead, every footfall placed with controlled silence, something unseen waiting beyond the treeline.

SWITCHBACK STRIDE — descending a steep switchback trail, walking staff planted firmly downslope with each step, pack riding high, boots raising faint dust on the dry stone path, the valley floor still a long way below her.

MAP AT THE CROSSROADS — seated on a flat boulder where two dirt roads divide, unfolded map spread across both knees, one finger tracing a route while the other arm props her upright, late dusk pressing in from the tree-line all around.

BOULDER SCRAMBLE — hands and boots fully committed to the top of a moss-slick granite boulder blocking the forest trail, mid-climb, weight shifting forward, pack swinging, the path resuming in full view on the other side just a reach away.

TAVERN WINDOW — settled into a worn bench beside a leaded-glass tavern window, one boot up on the opposite chair, ale-tankard wrapped in both hands and lifted halfway, watching rain streak the glass and the dark road beyond.

RIDGE WALK — moving along a narrow ridgeline in full stride, wind pressing her cloak flat against her side, staff angled out for balance, the drop falling away sharply on her left, a pale sky wide and indifferent overhead.

WHETSTONE BY CAMPFIRE — seated cross-legged just outside the firelight's full reach, long blade resting along her thigh, drawing a whetstone down the edge in slow deliberate strokes, sparks from the small camp behind her catching in her peripheral, dusk gone full dark around her.

ROPE BRIDGE CROSSING — one hand tight on the guide-rope, mid-span on a swaying rope bridge above a gorge, body braced into the movement, eyes fixed on the far bank, the river a grey ribbon far below her boots.

MOUNTED ON THE RIDGE — sitting tall in the saddle as her horse crests a forested ridge, reins loose in her lap, leaning forward slightly as the animal picks its footing on the loose stone, a pale morning sky breaking open ahead of them both.

LANTERN AT THE CAVE MOUTH — standing upright at the dark threshold of a cave entrance, arm extended, lantern held high and swinging slightly, yellow light spilling into the black passage just far enough to see the tunnel bend, everything beyond still hidden.

FALLEN TRUNK DUCK — mid-step beneath a massive fallen tree blocking the forest path, body low and forward-moving, one hand bracing the bark overhead for clearance, pack tucked, boots already landing on the far side, barely slowing her pace.

FOREST TRAIL STRIDE — walking a wide forest trail at a steady pace, walking staff swinging in countertime to her stride, light breaking in long columns through old-growth canopy above, the path stretching forward until it curves and disappears.

STEPPING-STONE FORD — balanced mid-stream on a slick stepping-stone, arms out slightly for balance, one boot just lifted for the next stone, cold water rushing close beneath her, the far bank a short leap ahead and the current pulling hard below.

WARY PRESS — back flat against a wide oak trunk at the trail's edge, dagger drawn and held point-up at her chest, head turned just enough to peer around the bark at the path ahead, absolute stillness, breath held.

VINE-DOOR PUSH — standing before a ruined stone doorway swallowed in hanging vines, one arm raised and pressing the curtain of growth aside, lantern in her other hand thrust through the gap, torchlight catching carved stonework just beyond the threshold.

TRAIL-BREAD LEAN — leaning back against a sun-warm boulder beside the trail, boots crossed at the ankle, one hand picking travel-bread apart slowly, eyes drifting up the valley she still has to cross, the rest deliberate, unhurried, earned.

DOWNHILL SCREE — picking carefully down a loose scree slope, pack bouncing with each short step, staff stabbing into the sliding stone for anchor, eyes tracking the firmer ground below, body angled slightly sideways to control the descent.

MAP TRACE IN CAMP — sitting on a log at the edge of camp, unfolded map weighted open with a stone and her knee, finger moving slowly along an inked river line, firelight low and warm at her back, morning still hours away.

LEADING MOUNT ACROSS — on foot at the head of the bridge, bridle in hand, coaxing her horse forward one step at a time onto the old stone span, the animal reading the footing carefully, her grip steady, river noise rising from below.

CRYSTAL PATH-LIGHT — paused on a dark stretch of forest trail well past dusk, one hand raised open-palmed, a small focus-crystal throwing pale blue light several strides forward onto the path, the trees pressing close on both sides, the road continuing ahead.

CLIFF-LEDGE EDGE — moving laterally along a narrow ledge carved into a cliff face, shoulder nearly touching the stone wall, free hand trailing the rock for feel, eyes ahead not down, the valley air open and cold at her back.

DUSK CAMP HANDS — crouched close to a small fire at the edge of camp, both hands spread toward the flame, cloak pulled tight, her pack sitting open behind her, the last light draining out of the sky above the dark treeline.

HIDDEN VISTA CREST — stepping up onto the final stone of a forested rise, the trees suddenly falling away, a hidden lake and ruined watchtower sprawled below her in the late-day light, one boot still on the last uphill step, breath caught.

RIDGE-CREST STRIDE — mid-stride at the top of a wind-scoured switchback, walking staff planted forward, pack riding her shoulders, eyes already scanning the valley below, the trail unwinding ahead like a question she intends to answer.

MAP STUDY — seated on a trailside boulder with the unfolded map spread across both knees, one finger tracing a route through inked mountain passes, the late sun cutting low through the pines, dusk arriving faster than expected.

FOREST TRAIL WALK — striding a packed-dirt forest trail with a walking staff swinging easy in her right hand, pack settled low, the canopy closing green overhead, a long road behind and the next waypoint still hours ahead.

CAMPFIRE WHETSTONE — sitting cross-legged beside a small crackling camp-fire at dusk, drawing a whetstone slowly up the length of her blade, the orange light catching each careful stroke, the dark forest pressing close beyond the firelight's edge.

MOUNTED RIDGE CREST — atop her horse at the highest point of a forested ridge, reins loose in one hand, head turning to read the land spread out below, the animal still and patient, the golden-hour light burning across the canopy.

VINE-PUSH DISCOVERY — standing in the gap of a ruined stone doorway, one forearm pressing aside a curtain of hanging vines, lantern raised in her other hand throwing orange light into the dark passage beyond, the threshold between known and unknown.

DAGGER STALKING — pressing her back flat against a broad oak trunk at the forest edge, dagger drawn and reversed low in her grip, head tilted listening, something moving just off-trail in the undergrowth ahead, not yet visible, not yet safe.

SCREE DESCENT — picking her way down a loose scree slope, staff angled back as a brake, each footfall sending small stones skittering, the mountain valley opening below, concentration absolute, the bottom of the descent still a long way down.

LANTERN PASSAGE MOUTH — standing upright at the black mouth of a hillside cave, lantern lifted to shoulder height, the warm beam pushing perhaps ten feet into the dark, one boot already crossing the threshold, the world inside still completely unknown.

TRAIL-MARKER CROSSROADS — standing at a weathered stone crossroads marker, one hand resting on its carved face, map held open at her side, comparing the chiselled place-names to her route, the four roads pulling in four directions under a grey sky.

BRIDGE CROSSING — walking a narrow stone bridge over a rushing gorge, one hand trailing the rough guide-rope strung along its edge, eyes forward, the river loud and white far below, the far bank offering a thin strip of trail and shadow.

CREEK-SIDE REST — sitting on a mossy bank with both boots off, feet trailing in the cold current of a slow stream, eating travel-bread from her pack with both hands, the afternoon light warm on her shoulders, the trail waiting patiently behind.

HORSE BRIDLE LEAD — leading her mount across a timber bridge by the bridle, her hand calm and low on the leather, the horse stepping careful on the planking, the river below grey and fast, both of them crossing together without hurry.

PALM-LIGHT CAVE — standing at the entrance to a low cave mouth, one hand raised with a soft glow pulsing from her open palm, the light reaching the first chamber walls and no further, her eyes already adjusting, her feet not yet moving inside.

GOLDEN-HOUR FOREST RIDE — riding a forest trail at a slow walk, the low evening sun slicing between the trunks and striping her and her horse in alternating gold and shadow, reins easy in one hand, the day almost spent, camp still ahead.

ROCK-STEP SCRAMBLE — hauling herself up a tall rock step that interrupts the trail, leading knee bent high onto the ledge, both hands pressing flat for lift, the path dropping away below and resuming on the higher plateau above, the next mile earned.

WARY FOREST CROUCH — advancing in a low slow crouch along a dim forest path, sword raised just off horizontal, point leading, gaze sweeping the shadows between the trees, something ahead has gone very still and she is matching its stillness with her own.

NIGHT CAMP FIRE-WARM — seated on a log at the edge of her small night-camp, both hands extended toward the low fire, breath visible in the cold air, the dark treeline forming a complete ring around the light, the long day behind her finally done.

CREEK-BANK REST — crouched low at a boulder-lined stream, waterskin submerged and one hand trailing in the cold current, afternoon light fracturing through alder canopy overhead, her boots off and drying on the bank behind her in easy silence.

DRAWN-BLADE STALK — advancing in a low crouch along a moss-floored forest corridor, short sword held level and steady at her side, eyes fixed on a dark gap between the trees ahead, breath held, the undergrowth utterly still and waiting.
